title: Panels & Floors
objective: Slice the twisted mass into floors and cut its facade into panels.
learn: Panelization: contouring a solid into floors and subdividing a surface by its UV domain.

nodes.need: a component that slices the mass into floors at a fixed spacing
nodes.hint: Intersect › Mathematical. Shape in, evenly spaced section curves out.
nodes.correct: Contour slices the closed mass with parallel planes every D units along the Z direction — one closed curve per floor.

wrong.divideCurve: Divide Curve splits a curve into points; it can't slice a solid.
wrong.series: Series gives you floor heights as numbers, but you'd still need to cut the mass at each one. Contour does both.
wrong.isotrim: Isotrim cuts a surface into patches — that's the panels, not the floors.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that slices the mass into floors at a fixed spacing.

nodes.need: a way to split the loft's UV space into a grid of panel cells
nodes.hint: Maths › Domain. A surface has a 2D (U×V) domain.
nodes.correct: Divide Domain² splits the loft surface's U×V domain into a grid of cells: U panels around, V panels up.

wrong.range: Range divides a 1D domain. A surface needs a 2D grid.
wrong.series: Series makes numbers, not UV cells.
wrong.divideCurve: Divide Curve works on curves, not surfaces.
wrong.*: This slot needs a way to split the loft's UV space into a grid of panel cells.

nodes.need: a component that cuts the facade surface into panels
nodes.hint: Surface › Util. One sub-surface per UV cell.
nodes.correct: Isotrim cuts one sub-surface per UV cell of the loft — the facade panels follow the twist.

wrong.contour: Contour already made the floors; panels need the surface cut by UV cells.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that cuts the facade surface into panels.

check.prompt: The Floor height slider should drive which input of Contour?
check.hint: S = shape, P = start point, N = direction, D = distance between contours.
check.correct: D is the spacing between contours — the floor-to-floor height.

wrong.S: S is the shape to slice; the tower mass is already connected.
wrong.P: P is the point where contouring starts — a location, not a spacing.
wrong.N: N is the slicing direction (a vector). Left empty it's Z, which gives horizontal floors.

check.prompt: Which input of Isotrim receives the Divide Domain² grid?
check.hint: S = surface to cut, D = domains to cut by.
check.correct: D takes the sub-domains: one surface × many cells = many panels.

wrong.S: S is the base surface; the loft is already connected.
wrong.*: That input isn't the domain list.
